source_title: USDA healthy food access case: Adelante Mujeres
unit_or_scope: Forest Grove Oregon Latino and immigrant farmers and low-income customers
direct_observation: 22-week farmer training and guaranteed market outlets used EBT and a 5 dollar SNAP match; weekly foot traffic nearly doubled from 800 to 1500 and EBT redemption rose 422 percent
closed_stage: culturally targeted fresh-food production and benefit route
missing_stage: household diet affordability health repeat participation and post-grant durability
evidence_status: official USDA case; project-period and program evidence
next_test: match customers to purchases prices diet and food-security follow-up

source_title: USDA Maine SNAP-Ed Tipped Trailer Co.
unit_or_scope: Newport Maine rural discount grocery and Penobscot County households
direct_observation: Discount retailer and Bangor Public Health used recipe-ingredient bundles and point-of-decision prompts in a county with low grocery access and elevated food insecurity
missing_stage: purchase completion price transport inventory diet quality health and durable security
evidence_status: official USDA SNAP-Ed report; intervention account not randomized outcome
next_test: track bundle purchases repeat use price and household food-security measures

unit_or_scope: low-income SNAP-eligible households early pandemic and online retailers
direct_observation: Online SNAP purchasing reduced food insufficiency in the study period; authorized retailers grew from 6 in July 2020 to 341 in September 2023 and online redemption reached 8.8 percent of benefits
missing_stage: delivery affordability substitutions cultural fit reliability and durable security
evidence_status: official USDA ERS analysis; early-pandemic study and aggregate expansion
next_test: link online orders delivery fees substitutions and household food-security outcomes

source_title: USDA Food on the Move Rhode Island SNAP incentive
unit_or_scope: Food on the Move customers and Rhode Island Eat Well Be Well policy route
direct_observation: Project reported 11 percent decline in inability to afford balanced healthy meals from baseline to 12 months; 77 percent shopped multiple times monthly and 88 percent reported positive experience
closed_stage: repeat use affordability perception and policy translation
missing_stage: same-household diet quality health causal counterfactual and long-term security
evidence_status: official USDA project account; self-selected evaluation evidence
next_test: follow participants and comparable nonparticipants through purchases diet health and security

missing_stage: complete trip affordability acceptable basket diet quality health and durable security
evidence_status: official ERS observational analysis; older non-causal sample
